summary: The root دحض (dHD) primarily means to slip, like a foot or the sun declining. It also metaphorically describes an argument becoming null or void, as if it slipped away from validity.
lane: 1 دَحَضَتْ رِجْلُهُ دحضت رجله دحضت رجلة , (S, A, K,) aor. دَحَضَ , (S,) inf. n. دَحْضٌ (S, A) and دُحُوضٌ , (A, TA,) His foot slipped. (S, A, K.) And دَحَضَ said of a man, He slipped. (Msb.) -b2- دَحَضَتِ الشَّمْسُ , (S, A, K,) aor. and inf. ns. as above, (TA,) (tropical:) The sun declined (S, A, K) towards the place of setting, (TA,) عَنْ كَبِدِ السَّمَآءُ (S) or عن بَطْنِ السمآء (A) [ from the meridian ]; as though it slipped. (TA.) -b3- دَحَضَتْ حُجَّتُهُ , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. دَحَضَ , (Msb,) inf. n. دُحُوضٌ , (S, K,) or دَحْضٌ , (Msb,) (tropical:) His argument, plea, allegation, or evidence, was, or became, null, or void. (S, A, * Msb, K.) -A2- See also 4, in two places.

headwords.def: دَحَضَتْ رِجْلُهُ دحضت رجله دحضت رجلة, (S, A, K,) aor. دَحَضَ, (S,) inf. n. دَحْضٌ (S, A) and دُحُوضٌ, (A, TA,) His foot slipped. (S, A, K.) And دَحَضَ said of a man, He slipped. (Msb.) دَحَضَتِ الشَّمْسُ, (S, A, K,) aor. and inf. ns. as above, (TA,) (tropical:) The sun declined (S, A, K) towards the place of setting, (TA,) عَنْ كَبِدِ السَّمَآءُ (S) or عن بَطْنِ السمآء (A) [ from the meridian ]; as though it slipped. (TA.) دَحَضَتْ حُجَّتُهُ, (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. دَحَضَ, (Msb,) inf. n.

ادحض أدحض ادحض دحض, (A, TA,) inf. n. إِدْحَاضٌ, (S,) He made (S, A, TA) a man's foot, (A, TA,) and a man, (TA,) to slip; (S, A, TA;) as also. (TA.) It (rain) made a place slippery. (TA.) (tropical:) He (God, S, Msb, or a man, K) annulled, or rendered null or void, an argument, a plea, an allegation, or an evidence: (S, Msb, K:) he rebutted it; as also, inf. n. دَحْضٌ. (TA; but in this instance, only the inf. n. of the latter verb is mentioned.) Thus in the Kur [xviii. 54, and xl.

دَحْضٌ دحض A slippery place; as also (S, K) and (O, K) and (Freytag, from the Deewán of the Hudhalees,) [or مَدْحَضٌ ?]: pl. دِحَاضٌ, (K,) [a pl. of the second,] like as جِبَالٌ is pl. of جَبَلٌ. (TA.) Also Water that causes slipping: pl. أَدْحَاضٌ. (TA.)
دَحَضٌ دحض: see the next preceding paragraph.
دَحُوضٌ دحوض: see the next preceding paragraph.

دَاحِضٌ داحض [ Slipping ] has for a pl. دُحْضٌ: occur- ring in a trad., in the phrase دُحْضُ الأَقْدَامِ, meaning (assumed tropical:) those having no firmness, or stability, nor determination, or resolution, in affairs. (TA.) حُجَّتُهُمْ دَاحِضَةٌ, in the Kur [xlii. 15], means (tropical:) Their argument, or plea, or allegation, is null, or void: or, as IDrd says, on the authority of AO; it means مَدْحُوضَةٌ [ rebutted ]. (TA.)

مَدْحَضَةٌ مدحضه مدحضة A cause of slipping; syn. مَزَلَّةٌ. (K.) You say, هٰ ِهِ مَدْحَضَةٌ لِلْقَدَمِ [ This is a cause of slipping to the foot ]. (A.) And مَكَانٌ مَدْحَضَةٌ, in a trad. respecting the Sirát, means A place on which the feet will not remain firm. (TA.)
مِدْحَاضٌ مدحاض A place in which one slips much, or often: pl. مَدَاحِضُ. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
